clue.text: Wide bowled by mistake into random bush

indicators.note: the run of cricket letters and the error is put into the word for random

parts.note: a stray shot or remark is random
W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wide
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A cricket ball, wide and bowled in error, flies off into some scrubby bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wide' and 'bowled' are cricket terms here, read as their scorecard letters; 'into' places the whole run inside the word for random.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit grows on a low plant gardeners loosely call a bush.

clue.text: Most of one's family raised one's identity

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters are read from the bottom up
most of signals the word losing its final letter

parts.note: your own flesh (and blood) is your family

explanation.surface: A person's sense of who they are comes largely from their relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last letter of FLESH to give FLES, and 'raised' turns that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's identity is their own ego or individual nature.

clue.text: Someone getting torn up about unfilled cannelloni baked dish

indicators.note: about means the torn word goes round the other letters

parts.note: rent is an old word for torn apart

indicators.note: unfilled pasta keeps only its outer shell, the first and last letters

parts.note: a pie is a dish baked in an oven

explanation.surface: A diner receives a pasta bake with the cannelloni ripped open and empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfilled' keeps just the shell of cannelloni, its first and last letters; 'about' wraps the torn word round them and the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone receiving something is a receiver of it, the getter.

clue.text: Remove with force or with ease

parts.note: rest is ease or relaxation

explanation.surface: Something can be taken out roughly or gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link here: the definition is 'Remove with force', and 'with ease' then builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something away violently or by twisting is exactly to take it by force.

clue.text: There's not a million in one shilling without first being frugal

indicators.note: in signals that the negation and million letters sit inside the other word
without first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: one acting as a shill, a planted lure, is a decoy
no means not
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A thrifty person would never have a fortune in a single old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shilling' is not the old coin but a verb: a shill lures buyers. 'without first' drops its first letter, and 'in' puts 'not a million' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift, careful use of money, is the noun for the state of spending little.

clue.text: Bound labourer aboard the ship turned brace

indicators.note: turned means the whole assembly is read backwards
aboard puts the labourer inside the word for the ship

parts.note: a ship is traditionally called she, so the ship is her
a serf was a labourer bound to the land

explanation.surface: A worker tied to a vessel turns round and grips a support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' puts the labourer inside the ship's pronoun, and 'turned' then reads the whole thing upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To brace someone is to invigorate them, as bracing sea air does.

clue.text: Mass with vessel from Bible gospel

parts.note: M is the scientific symbol for mass
Noah's ark is a vessel

explanation.surface: A church service involving a vessel drawn from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four New Testament gospels carries the name of its evangelist author.

clue.text: A mountain parrot biting large leader of pack

indicators.note: biting has the parrot's word close its jaws round the other letter

parts.note: the kea is a mountain parrot of New Zealand
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A mountain bird attacks the head of a group of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The kea is a New Zealand alpine parrot; 'biting' puts L inside KEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult who leads a Cub Scout pack takes this title, from the wolf in The Jungle Book.

clue.text: Under mayor Livingstone, say, serenade North London district

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means these letters come below the mayor's name

parts.note: Ken Livingstone was the first Mayor of London
to serenade someone is to sing to them
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Under a particular mayor, a part of North London was serenaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone was Mayor of London 2000-08; 'Under' places SING TO and N below KEN in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known borough area of west London, home to the palace and museums.

clue.text: English empiricist mostly denied freedom of movement?

indicators.note: mostly signals the word losing its final letter

parts.note: someone locked up is denied freedom of movement

explanation.surface: A British philosopher of experience was largely kept from moving about.
explanation.definitionFit: John, the seventeenth-century philosopher, founded British empiricism.

clue.text: Fence's for changing when not being filmed

indicators.note: changing means the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden fence gets altered while the cameras are off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done out of the camera's view happens away from the filmed picture.

clue.text: Minion caught more bleak across lake

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: across has the bleak word stretch across, enclosing the other letter

parts.note: raw weather is bleak, so rawer is more bleak
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A servant got caught in harsher weather out on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A fawning toady, a sycophantic underling, is called this informally.

clue.text: Hazard in road even if in lines protected by stanchion

indicators.note: protected by puts the poetic word inside the upright

parts.note: a stanchion is an upright pole
tho is the clipped form of though used in verse lines

explanation.surface: A road danger even when it is lined and guarded by a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in lines' means in poetry, where THO stands for though, 'even if'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit in the road surface is a hazard to drivers and cyclists.

clue.text: Some defamation for family of workers on the fiddle?

definitions.text: family of workers on the fiddle?

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Slander directed at a family of crooks working a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' suggests fraud, but here it means making violins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cremona family were famous violin makers, so they worked on the fiddle.

clue.text: Jailbird was a pest online, under supervision

parts.note: a con is a convict, a jailbird
to troll is to make a nuisance of oneself online

explanation.surface: A prisoner who made trouble on the internet is now monitored.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept in check and regulated is under supervision.

clue.text: Give more than enough annually, dividing nothing particularly

parts.note: O is nought, nothing

indicators.note: dividing puts the yearly abbreviation between letters of the other word

parts.note: very means particularly
PA is per annum, annually

explanation.surface: Handing over too much every year while splitting nothing in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: To remunerate excessively is to give more money than is due.

clue.text: Variety of tones from female chum?

parts.note: a pal is a chum
-ette is a suffix marking a female, as in usherette

explanation.surface: A range of voices or colours coming from a woman friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word: a female chum would be a pal-ette.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's board holds a range of colours, a variety of tones.

clue.text: Norse goddess, transcendental, with no good portion

parts.note: Hel is the Norse goddess of the underworld
pi is a transcendental number

explanation.surface: A Norse deity, other-worldly and useless, gets a share.
explanation.definitionFit: A serving of food is a portion.

clue.text: Brings on something with small charge for attack

parts.note: to incur something is to bring it on oneself
an ion is a particle carrying a small electric charge

explanation.surface: Something with a minor charge prompts an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid into enemy territory is a form of attack.

clue.text: Honorary point, lacking ne plus ultra, invalidated

indicators.note: lacking means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: a tine is a point or prong of a fork
the letters ne as written are removed

indicators.note: invalidated means the word is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An honorary title loses its ultimate point and is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ne plus ultra' looks like the Latin phrase for the utmost but splits up: 'lacking' removes ne from the prong word, 'plus' joins, and 'invalidated' shuffles ultra.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular post is held in name only, as an honorary position is.

clue.text: Remains to be housed around university

indicators.note: around puts the word for housed around the abbreviation

parts.note: to reside is to be housed or to live somewhere

explanation.surface: Students stay put, living around their university.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over after a process is its leftovers or remains.

clue.text: Gentleman taking company in two directions, in a blow to Italy?

indicators.note: taking means the title picks up the company letters next to it

parts.note: sir is how a gentleman is addressed

indicators.note: in two directions means the abbreviation is written backwards and then forwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, here as OC then CO

explanation.surface: A knight takes his firm north and south, a setback for Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blow' is a wind, not a setback: this hot wind blows from North Africa into Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot, dusty Saharan wind that reaches southern Italy is literally a blow to it.

clue.text: Member of military class laid waste in Masuria

indicators.note: laid waste means the letters of the region are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier from the warrior caste ravaged a region of Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: Masuria is a lake district in north-east Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan's hereditary warrior caste belonged to a military class.

clue.text: Men with tool for drilling socket

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers or men
a drill bit bores the hole

explanation.surface: Workers with a drill making a hole for a fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'socket' looks like an electrical fitting, but here it is the eye socket.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony cavity holding the eye is called its orbit.

clue.text: Inlet in Orleans, or marshy water in New Orleans?

parts.note: a bay is a sea inlet
ou is the French word for or, as spoken in Orleans

explanation.surface: A creek near the French city of Orleans, or swampy water in Louisiana.
explanation.walkthrough: Orleans is a French city, so 'or' there is French OU.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow marshy creek of the Louisiana delta is a characteristic Louisiana waterway.

clue.text: Sister keeps copious specimen collection

indicators.note: keeps means the sister's abbreviation holds the other word inside

parts.note: ample means copious

explanation.surface: A nun holds onto a large collection of specimens.
explanation.definitionFit: An embroidered sampler shows a collection of stitch specimens.

clue.text: Allowed in charge, having landed outside

indicators.note: outside has the word for landed going round the other letters

parts.note: a bird that has lit on a branch has landed

explanation.surface: Permission granted to someone in command once they have touched down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lawful and permitted is allowed.

clue.text: Leave note in blood

parts.note: to go is to leave
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Abandon a message written in blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Shed or clotted blood, as in a gory horror film, is gore.

clue.text: Pioneer to secure Scottish port and volunteer for service?

indicators.note: to secure has the pioneer's word holding the port inside it

parts.note: a pioneer is a leader
Ayr is a port on Scotland's west coast

explanation.surface: A trailblazer captures a Scottish harbour and signs up to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is a church service, not military duty.
explanation.definitionFit: An unordained person who volunteers to lead parts of church services.

clue.text: African city's stone pile finally moved on a place?

indicators.note: the final letter is moved on one place in the alphabet, swapped for the next letter

parts.note: a cairn is a pile of stones

explanation.surface: An African city's heap of stones ends up shifted to another spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved on a place' means the last letter N becomes the next letter of the alphabet, O.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Egypt is a major city of North Africa.

clue.text: Perhaps an upper Republican approved interns

indicators.note: interns means the word for approved confines the other letter within it

parts.note: to dig something is slang for approving of it

explanation.surface: A Republican gave the nod to some interns, maybe to a senior one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interns' is a verb, imprisons; 'an upper' is a stimulant.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulant pill, slang upper, is one example of a narcotic.

clue.text: Rebels rise violently against point of view

indicators.note: violently means the word is churned into a new order

parts.note: a stance is a point of view

explanation.surface: Insurgents rise up fiercely against a particular viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground movement fighting an occupier is called this collectively, as the French one was.
